rows.lead: You are seeing 17.6% of your market.
rows.angle: You are seeing 17.6% of your market. The median PE firm covers 17.6% of relevant deal flow; top quartile 27.5%. Boutique LMM advisors: 11.8%.

rows.lead: Thousands contacted. One close.
rows.angle: Thousands contacted. One close. Stanford: thousands → ~50 visits → ~10 LOIs → 1 close. IESE: 3,000 explored, 159 owner conversations, ~4 LOIs. Carry both, don't average.

rows.lead: Financing stopped killing deals. Diligence started.
rows.angle: Financing stopped killing deals. Diligence started. Non-QoE findings 25.3% + QoE discrepancies 21.3% = ~47%. Financing breaks fell 21.3% → 10.7%.

rows.lead: Family offices walk at 37 days. PE takes 106.
rows.angle: Family offices walk at 37 days. PE takes 106. Days under exclusivity before a broken deal died. The spread is the story.

rows.lead: The silver tsunami is a backlog, not a flood.
rows.angle: The silver tsunami is a backlog, not a flood. $10T and 12M businesses are over-aggregated; defensible is ~2.9M employer firms with 55+ owners. Gallup: 67% of owners 55+ intend to close or are unsure.

rows.lead: What a BD hire actually costs before it sources anything.
rows.angle: What a BD hire actually costs before it sources anything. $150K–$250K all-in, plus a data stack that clears $100K/yr in overlapping subscriptions.

rows.lead: Thirty percent of PE firms had nobody doing this.
rows.angle: Thirty percent of PE firms had nobody doing this. SPS 2021: ~70% had at least one BD professional. The figure is four years old and SPS stopped publishing it.

rows.lead: Nobody publishes time-to-first-sourced-deal.
rows.angle: Nobody publishes time-to-first-sourced-deal. The one number that would settle the make-vs-buy argument does not exist. Argument only.

rows.lead: The hybrid answer, including from the people selling the alternative.
rows.angle: The hybrid answer, including from the people selling the alternative. DueDilio concedes outsourcing "is generally not recommended to completely replace internal efforts." Meet the objection.

rows.lead: Distributions are running at ~6% of AUM against a ~16% historical average.
rows.angle: Distributions are running at ~6% of AUM against a ~16% historical average. And the "~14% of NAV" version circulating conflates a ten-year average with the current year.

rows.lead: 12,552 PE-backed companies. Eight to nine years of exits at current rates.
rows.angle: 12,552 PE-backed companies. Eight to nine years of exits at current rates.

rows.lead: Deployment pressure doesn't buy platforms. It buys add-ons.
rows.angle: Deployment pressure doesn't buy platforms. It buys add-ons. And add-ons are exactly what the intermediated channel covers worst.

rows.lead: SBA changed the arithmetic on 1 June 2025.
rows.angle: SBA changed the arithmetic on 1 June 2025. A seller note counts toward equity only on full standby for the loan term, capped at half the injection — 5% of a 10% requirement.

rows.lead: Buy at 5.9x, build to 10.0x.
rows.angle: Buy at 5.9x, build to 10.0x. $10M–$25M TEV against $100M–$250M. The size gradient is the whole LMM thesis, and it is an origination problem.
